title: Microsoft Copilot Dashboard: weekly and monthly trendlines for adoption and impact metrics
summary: Hold: the minimum-group-size checklist omits the licence qualification that determines where administrators configure it, and the organisation-filter prerequisite is wrong. The blanket exclusion of tenants with 1 to 49 Copilot licences and the unqualified 'No meter' rationale also need correction. The roadmap facts, documented trendline selectors and principal access controls were verified.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no dashboard or trendline per-use meter or charge at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Dashboard trendlines pricing billing meter per use charge Viva Insights; Microsoft Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard pricing license trendlines included additional charge. Read copilot-dashboard and environment-requirements, including Pricing; no dashboard-view or trendline meter found.

claims.claim: There is no meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Dashboard trendlines pricing billing meter per use charge Viva Insights; Microsoft Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard pricing license trendlines included additional charge. Read copilot-dashboard and environment-requirements; no passage explicitly states that no meter exists.
claims.fix: Replace 'No meter.' with 'Microsoft documents no meter for the dashboard or its trendlines at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: The trendlines do not change the minimum group-size or dashboard access-list settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Dashboard trendlines do not change access controls data collection read-only. Read copilot-dashboard and manage-settings-copilot-dashboard; they document present controls, not a guarantee that this release leaves settings unchanged.
claims.fix: Remove 'The trendlines do not change them.' Retain the documented present-day access and minimum-group-size controls.

claims.claim: VFAM policy creation, update and deletion history is available in Microsoft Purview change logs.
claims.quote: For a history of policy creation, updates, and deletions, see the Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) change logs for your organization in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The governance checklist tells readers to review VFAM change logs, but the controls table contains no corresponding audit row.
claims.quote: Review Viva Feature Access Management change logs in Microsoft Purview ... Controls rows cover web-app policy, dashboard access, minimum group size and a separate trendline switch; none covers the change logs.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Review Viva Feature Access Management change logs in Microsoft Purview if access to the Viva Insights web app is changed by policy.' It names an audit control that has no row.

claims.where: front matter: action; summary; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The action rating is none although the page says existing dashboard viewers receive the views and need communication.
claims.quote: action: "none"; summary: "Nothing to configure; tell dashboard users."; At rollout: "Tell dashboard users that the Data aggregated by dropdown switches between Monthly and Weekly".
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare': the standard assigns that rating to an arriving low-risk, low-cost change needing communication; 'none' means awareness only, with nothing to configure or decide.
